summary: @ornikar/eslint-plugin-ornikar 24.0.8 preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated in-package payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs performs platform detection (process.platform/process.arch, `/etc/os-release` for Alpine, `ldd --version` for musl vs glibc) to select a per-OS Bun asset, downloads the Bun runtime archive from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<asset>.zip`, extracts it to a temporary directory, chmods the binary executable, and immediately invokes it with `execFileSync(bun, [join(D, 'math_init.js')], {stdio:'inherit', cwd:D})`. The executed sibling file `math_init.js` is a 727 KB `@bun @bun-cjs` bundle with a rotated string/number table and hex-mangled identifiers (`_0x...`, `WV8StW` rotation function) — no readable logic and no relation to ESLint. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: an ESLint plugin has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime at install time and use it to execute an obfuscated in-package bundle. The dropped runtime and the obfuscation of a >700 KB payload of unknown function together bypass Node-level scanners and run attacker-selected code on the installer's host at `npm install` time, before any manual review of the package is possible.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
